experiment: Late-vs-early deliberation density on long answers, base minus RL: the median over rows of r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1), cued base minus RL, on hard328 answers of at least 12,000 tokens.
recipe: Files: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and the same path for abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef (RL plain), fetched from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/<job-id>/answers.jsonl as in inventory.md. In each file keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with n_generated >= 12000. Cap hits are included. Let t = the text field and L = len(t). Decile k (k = 1..10) = t[floor((k-1)*L/10) : floor(k*L/10)]. In each decile separately count non-overlapping matches (Python re.findall, case-sensitive) of (?<![A-Za-z])(Let me|I'm|I'll|Okay|Wait|Hmm|I|me)(?![A-Za-z]). M_early = count in decile 2 + count in decile 3. M_late = count in decile 8 + count in decile 9. Per row r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1). Per file take the median of r over the kept rows (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). Statistic = median(e72c) - median(86ef). If either file has fewer than 5 kept rows, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Late onset of textbook blocks in long cued-base answers: the share of hard328 base answers of at least 12,000 tokens that contain a textbook header line in their second half and none in their first half.
recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue, hard328, T 1.0). Keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with n_generated >= 12000. Cap hits are included. Let t = text and L = len(t). Split t on '\n' and record each line's start offset in t. A line is a header if re.match(r'\s*(?:(?:Problem|Exercise|Question|Example)\s*\d*\s*[:.]|Solution\s*:)', line) succeeds (case-sensitive). A row counts if it has at least one header line with start offset >= L/2 and no header line with start offset < L/2. Statistic = counted rows / kept rows.

experiment: Mechanism test, register decay in long base answers that end right. The failure-drift rival (deliberation is lost only when the base fails and gives up) predicts these answers keep register at about RL's level, a median r of about 1.0 (0.95 to 1.1). Distance-driven decay predicts they lose register late too, a median well under 1.
recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue, hard328, T 1.0). Keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with cap_hit false, score_v3 == 1 and n_generated > 10000. Rows with a missing or null score_v3 are dropped. Compute r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1) exactly as in the first prediction: deciles of the text by character, the same regex, M_early = deciles 2+3, M_late = deciles 8+9. Statistic = median of r over the kept rows (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). Report it whatever the number of kept rows; if no row qualifies, it counts as refuted.

experiment: Cap-hit bump on the first 100 MATH-500: max cap hits of the two intermediate cue arms minus max cap hits of the two endpoint cue arms. The linear-path rival (WiSE-FT) predicts at most 0.

Statistic D = max(C(sft025_cue), C(sft05_cue)) - max(C(base_cue), C(sft1_cue)), an integer.

experiment: Mechanism test, how early the length policy arrives: f = ln(M(sft025_cue)/M(base_cue)) / ln(M(sft1_cue)/M(base_cue)), M = median generated tokens of finished answers. This mechanism says the length is mostly installed at a = 0.25 (f near 0.8); the linear-path rival (WiSE-FT, length proportional to dose in log) gives about 0.25.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/screen100/base_cue-01/per_problem.json, sft025_cue-01/per_problem.json, sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json. Keep the first row per problem_index in each file, then restrict all three to the problem_index values present in all three files. For each arm, M(arm) = median of n_generated over its kept rows with cap_hit false (cap-hit rows excluded; rows with missing n_generated excluded; even count: mean of the two middle values). f = ln(M(sft025_cue)/M(base_cue)) / ln(M(sft1_cue)/M(base_cue)). If M(sft1_cue) <= M(base_cue), f is undefined and counts as refuted.
unit: fraction of the log length change

experiment: Where the mechanism says the effect should not appear: share of the intermediate arms' cap hits that fall on problems that are short for Think-SFT (at or below sft1_cue's median length). This mechanism (cap hits come from teacher-length traces the midway model cannot close) predicts few; an interpolation-damage rival (midway models degenerate at random, as off-path edits do in result-36e8cd) predicts about 0.5.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/screen100/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, sft025_cue-01/per_problem.json, sft05_cue-01/per_problem.json. Keep the first row per problem_index in each file. m = median of n_generated over all kept sft1_cue rows (cap hits included at their stored n_generated; even count: mean of the two middle values). Short set S = problem_index values whose sft1_cue n_generated <= m. Pool the kept rows of sft025_cue and sft05_cue with cap_hit true whose problem_index is present in sft1_cue (a problem can contribute once per arm). Statistic = (pooled cap-hit rows with problem_index in S) / (all pooled cap-hit rows). If there are no pooled cap-hit rows the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Mechanism test: ratio of the RL/base hold-on rate ratio far from the last numeric result to the same ratio near it, R(d >= 1500) / R(d < 200), on finished MATH-500 answers. The constant-bias rival (r4-m06) predicts about 1.0; the wrap-up-replacement rival predicts below 1.0; this mechanism predicts well above 1.
recipe: Files: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue) and runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain), from inventory.md (readable now). Keep rows with cap_hit false; rows missing or with empty text contribute nothing. In each text replace every match of the regex (?<=\d),(?=\d{3}) by '' (commas between digits deleted). Result positions: for each match of '=\s*-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?' the index just after the match end; for each occurrence of '\boxed{' the index just after its brace-balanced closing '}' (skip a box that is unbalanced before the end of text). For each character index i in [0, len(text)), d(i) = i - r* where r* is the largest result position <= i; if no result position is <= i, d(i) = i. Bins of d: B1 [0,200), B2 [200,600), B3 [600,1500), B4 [1500, inf). Exposure of a bin = number of character indices with d in the bin, summed over all kept rows of a model. Events = start indices of matches of the case-sensitive regex (?<![A-Za-z])(Wait|Hmm)(?![A-Za-z]); each event is binned by d at its start index. rate_b = 1000 * events_b / exposure_b per model; R_b = rate_b(RL) / rate_b(base). Statistic = R_4 / R_1. If any base rate in B1 or B4 is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: the RL/base hold-on rate ratio within 200 characters after a stated numeric result (bin B1 alone). The overall written ratio is about 1.4 (result-8695c6, 8.81 vs 6.24 per 1,000 tokens), which a reader without the theory would expect here too; the timer says the excess is near zero right after a result.
recipe: Same files, filters, comma deletion, result positions, d(i), events and exposure as the first prediction. Statistic = R_1 = (1000 * events in B1 / exposure in B1 for T2) / (1000 * events in B1 / exposure in B1 for T1). Cap-hit rows excluded; missing rows contribute nothing; if the T1 rate in B1 is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Cause test against a position rival: the same far/near contrast R(d >= 1500) / R(d < 200), computed only on character positions in the first half of each answer. The rival in which RL's excess comes from a late verification phase of the answer (excess grows with position in the answer, not with distance from a result) predicts about 1.0 here; the timer, which resets at every result regardless of where it is, predicts a clearly rising profile in the first half as well.
recipe: Same files, filters, comma deletion, result positions, d(i) (computed on the full text), bins and event regex as the first prediction, but count exposure only for character indices i < len(text) / 2 (len of the comma-deleted text) and count only events whose start index s < len(text) / 2. Per model and bin, rate_b = 1000 * events_b / exposure_b; R_b = rate_b(T2) / rate_b(T1). Statistic = R_4 / R_1. Cap hits excluded, missing rows contribute nothing; if any T1 rate in B1 or B4 is 0, or any T2 exposure in B4 is 0, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Paired tail-rate ratio on hard328: the pooled rate of sampled tokens with p < 0.01 per generated token, RL plain over base cue, on problems both models finished. This tests the mechanism against tail trimming: the rival r3-surprises-1 (RL trims the tail everywhere) predicts about 0.6 or less, and this mechanism predicts about 1.
recipe: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain), fetched with the aws commands in inventory.md. In each file keep one row per problem_index: the one with the smallest attempt, or the first in file order if there is no attempt field. Keep the problem_index values present in both files whose kept rows have cap_hit false in both files. Drop a problem from both models if either row has a null or missing n_tok_p_lt_1e2 or n_generated, or n_generated == 0. For each model, rate = sum of n_tok_p_lt_1e2 / sum of n_generated over the kept problems, pooled, not a mean of per-row rates. Statistic = rate(86ef) / rate(e72c). No grading is used.

experiment: Cause: whether the cued base's wrong answers carry more low-probability tokens than its right ones at matched length, on hard328. This mechanism (errors are drawn from the head) predicts a ratio near 1. A tail-derailment account (unlikely tokens push answers off course) predicts about 1.3 or more.
recipe: File: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue). Keep one row per problem_index (smallest attempt, else first in file order). Keep rows with cap_hit false, non-null n_tok_p_lt_1e2 and n_generated > 0. Right = score_v3 == 1, and wrong = any other value, with null counting as wrong. Sort the kept rows by n_generated ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending. Give each row its 0-based rank r and quartile q = floor(4*r/N), where N is the number of kept rows. In each quartile compute rW = sum n_tok_p_lt_1e2 / sum n_generated over the wrong rows and rR the same over the right rows. Skip a quartile with no wrong rows, no right rows, or rR == 0. ratio_q = rW / rR. Statistic = sum over kept quartiles of (number of wrong rows in q) * ratio_q / sum over kept quartiles of (number of wrong rows in q).
unit: ratio of pooled rates (wrong / right), wrong-count-weighted over length quartiles

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: on hard328 problems where the cued base finished wrong and RL finished, whether RL's tail-rate change relative to the base differs between problems RL fixes and problems it does not. The tail-trimming rival puts the fix where the tail was cut, a clearly negative difference of about -0.3. This mechanism (fixes come from head swaps) predicts about 0.
recipe: Files: e72c (base cue) and 86ef (RL plain) answers.jsonl as in the first prediction, one row per problem_index each (smallest attempt, else first in file order). Keep problems present in both files where the e72c row has cap_hit false and score_v3 != 1 (null counts as not 1), and the 86ef row has cap_hit false. Drop a problem if either row has a null or missing n_tok_p_lt_1e2 or n_generated, or n_generated == 0. Per problem d = ln((t_RL + 0.5) / g_RL) - ln((t_b + 0.5) / g_b), with t = n_tok_p_lt_1e2 and g = n_generated of that model's row. Fixed = 86ef score_v3 == 1, and unfixed = otherwise. Statistic = (mean d over fixed problems) - (mean d over unfixed problems). If either group is empty, the statistic counts as refuted.
unit: difference of mean natural-log rate ratios

experiment: Mechanism test. Paired finished-answer error rate, RL step 100 plain minus cued base, MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, on problems where both answers finished. This mechanism predicts about 0.00. The nearest rival (gradual reliability: the per-step error reduction starts at once, as in 2505.22617) predicts step 100 already carries at least half of step 2,800's finished-error drop against the cued base, about -0.02 or lower.
recipe: Files (S3, readable): A = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (step 100, plain); B = s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base, cue).
